open-question.question: What does the body of a `Task-completion:` commit hold beyond the acceptance bar's `- ` bullets, given that today's `TASKS_DONE.md` entry records both the task's brief and the bar under a `**Verified:**` label, and that once the file is gone the brief survives only as the removed lines of `TASKS_TODO.md` in that commit's own diff?

How does the inline `complete-task` skill's one fixed shell call hand the multi-line acceptance bar to the commit tool's `--body` argument, given that criteria routinely hold backticks, double quotes, and apostrophes, which a double-quoted shell argument would expand or break on, and that the commit tool's contract gains no body-file option?

Once `remove` reads no bar, which step refuses an empty acceptance bar, or an absent or empty body file after an agent's `DONE`, before a `Task-completion:` commit lands, given that today only the task-list tool's `move` refuses an empty bar, the commit tool makes a subject-only commit from an empty body, and the orchestrator stops the run only on an absent or empty path file?

Where is the acceptance bar's record form (one `- ` bullet per criterion, in verification order, held verbatim from derivation) stated once the completion procedure's step 5 command is a bare `remove` that carries no bar, given that the procedure stays commit-free and the bar's only destination is each runner's own commit?
open-question.alternative: The record form (one `- ` bullet per criterion, in verification order, written as each stood when it passed, neither re-derived nor summarized) stays stated once, in `core/shared/complete-procedure.md`, as prose beside the bare `remove` at step 5 (or folded into step 2's hold-it-verbatim sentence), worded as the form of the bar the procedure hands to the runner, with the destination named only as "the record your runner's own file writes" and no git step, commit, or body named. The inline `complete-task` skill's fixed call and the agent's body-file heredoc show the bar as `- ` bullet placeholders and refer to the procedure for the form, adding no prose rule of their own. Keeps one home for a rule both runners share, in the file both already read and follow, so the form cannot drift between the inline and the isolated commit, and the procedure's commit-free contract holds because a text form is not a git step. The procedure describes the shape of a record whose destination it may not name, so the sentence reads abstractly and a runner learns where the bullets land only from its own file; if the commit body is to hold more than the bar (a sibling question's axis), the procedure states only part of the body's shape and the rest lives elsewhere.

The procedure keeps only step 2's derive-and-hold-verbatim rule and step 5's bare `remove`, saying nothing of the record form; the form is stated in each runner's own file, beside the fixed call that writes it: the inline `complete-task` skill's call that passes the bar as its commit's body, and the `complete-task` agent's heredoc that writes the bar to its second fixed-name scratch file, each with a matching sentence (one `- ` bullet per criterion, in verification order, verbatim), as the agent's path-file sentence already restates the commit procedure's literal-path rule. Puts the form where the bar is actually written, next to the destination it shapes, so the commit-free procedure carries nothing about a record it no longer writes and each runner's file shows its complete call and its rule together. The same rule has two homes kept in matching wording by hand, the duplication the shared procedures exist to avoid, and nothing tests that the two sentences agree, so the inline and agent bodies can diverge silently; it also couples the form to how each runner hands the bar over, which sibling questions are still settling.

The record form is added to `core/shared/task-format.md`, the existing single home of the task-list format, as a section on the completed task's verified bar (one `- ` bullet per criterion, in verification order, verbatim from derivation), and the completion procedure and both runners point at it; the procedure stays commit-free and the runners' fixed calls show bullet placeholders only. Keeps one home in a file that already owns the format of everything recorded about a task, so the brief's shape and the bar's shape are found together and no new shared file is added. `task-format.md` is the authoring contract `derive-tasks` and `submit-task` follow, and the invariants keep the bar's form deliberately apart from authoring so it is never read as one; placing it there invites an authoring runner to write acceptance bullets into a brief, the `Steps`/`Success` creep the task-altitude invariant forbids, and loads a rule the two authoring runners never use.

A new shared file, for example `core/shared/bar-format.md`, becomes the one home of the record form (one `- ` bullet per criterion, in verification order, verbatim from derivation), referenced by the completion procedure at step 2 and by both runners at their fixed calls; the procedure stays commit-free and no other file restates the rule. Gives the form one named, explicit home that sits apart from both the authoring contract and the commit-free procedure, and gives the milestones tool's body reader and any later writer of the body a single place to read the contract from. A whole shared file for two or three sentences, adding one more read to every completion agent's run and one more cross-reference to keep in step, where the procedure both runners already follow could hold the same sentences; the CLAUDE.md layout entry, the build, and the docs gain a file for a rule that never needed one before.

No prose states the record form anywhere: the procedure keeps step 2's rule that the bar is held verbatim and must not drift, step 5 shrinks to the bare `remove`, and the form is carried only by the `- ` bullet placeholders shown in each runner's fixed call (the inline skill's body and the agent's body-file heredoc), with "in verification order" and "neither re-derived nor summarized into prose" dropped as stated rules. The least prose to write and keep consistent: the placeholders runners copy already fix one bullet per criterion, and the verbatim hold survives at step 2, so nothing has to be placed in a home that names no destination. The ordering rule and the ban on summarizing into prose are lost, so bodies can arrive reordered or as a prose paragraph, which the milestones tool's `tasks` body print and every reader of it (finish's summary, `ask-in-milestone-context`) then show inconsistently across tasks; the record form becomes an implication of a placeholder rather than a rule a runner can be held to.

open-question.question: Which fields does one line of the milestones tool's `tasks` query carry, in what order and with what separator, given that the draft lists date, milestone path, and task title, that a title may hold spaces, and that a reader wanting a task's diff needs its commit hash or must search subjects itself?

When `tasks` runs with its body flag, how is each commit's body set apart from the task lines around it so a reader can tell where one task's bar ends and the next task begins, including how a task whose commit carries no body (one completed before the bar moved into commits) appears?

How does `tasks` assign a milestone to a `Task-completion:` commit whose file list holds no `TASKS_TODO.md` under a milestone directory, or more than one, given that two commits in this repository's log also touch a fixture `TASKS_TODO.md` under `tests/fixtures/`?

Does `tasks` read only commits whose subject opens with `Task-completion:`, or also the 222 retired `Tasklist-completion: complete one milestone task` commits that carry the task heading in their body?

What does `tasks` print, and with what exit status, for a PATH no task commit ever touched, whether a live milestone with no completed task or a mistyped path, given that git's path-scoped log prints nothing for either without distinguishing them?
How does `tasks` behave in a shallow clone, whose truncated log would silently omit older task commits from what it prints, given that the draft names a shallow clone as a limit a stop line says?

Which of the five readers that replace their `TASKS_DONE.md` read with a `tasks` call (`finish-current-milestone`, `derive-tasks`, `ask-in-milestone-context`, `submit-task`, `discuss-new-task`) run it with the body flag, reading each task's bar, and which read task titles alone?

When a reader's `tasks` call fails (the tool refusing, or git unavailable), do `finish-current-milestone` and `derive-tasks` stop on a fixed line of their own, or proceed without the completed-task record?

Which mentions of `TASKS_DONE.md` outside the runtime files, host templates, docs, and tests the goal names are rewritten in this milestone, in particular the pull request template's checklist item and the three passages of `ideas/benchmark_for_cairn.md` that describe a cairn chain's tree?
